gloss: to have a good eye for, to be discerning

definitions.gloss: to have a good eye for, to be discerning
definitions.explanation: To have the ability to recognize quality, value, or authenticity; to be a good judge of something.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{骨董品|こっとうひん}に{目|め}が{利|き}く。
examples.english: She has a good eye for antiques.

examples.japanese: {目|め}の{利|き}く{人|ひと}に{見|み}てもらおう。
examples.english: Let's have someone with a discerning eye take a look.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{経験|けいけん}で、{良|よ}い{品|しな}に{目|め}が{利|き}くようになった。
examples.english: Through years of experience, I've developed an eye for quality goods.

notes:
{目|め}が{利|き}く literally means "one's eyes work well" and describes the ability to judge quality or value accurately. It implies trained expertise rather than innate talent.

USAGE:
Often used for expertise in evaluating:
- {骨董品|こっとうひん} (antiques)
- {美術品|びじゅつひん} (art)
- {宝石|ほうせき} (gems)
- {人材|じんざい} (talent/personnel)
- {食材|しょくざい} (ingredients)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～に{目|め}が{利|き}く: to have a good eye for ~
- {目|め}の{利|き}く{人|ひと}: a discerning person

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {目利|めき}き: a connoisseur, an expert judge (noun form)
- {目|め}が{肥|こ}えている: to have refined taste (from broad exposure)
- {見|み}る{目|め}がある: to have good judgment (more general)
